back: Parents and children plus other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins, sharing responsibilities.
A household in which a child under 18 runs the home and cares for siblings, usually after parents die or leave.
Monogamous: one husband, one wife. Polygamous (polygynous): one husband, two or more wives.
A family in which one parent brings up the children (death, divorce, separation, work away or never married).

front: Name three roles of children in the home.
back: Respect and obey elders; help with chores; study; care for younger siblings and elderly relatives.

front: Name three roles of family members in the nation.
back: Raise law-abiding citizens; pay taxes and vote; produce goods and food; pass on national heritage.

front: Why have grandparents' roles grown in many families?
back: Parents migrate to towns or abroad for work, leaving grandparents to bring up the children.

front: Can a family be polygamous and extended at once?
back: Yes: marriage type (mono/polygamous) and household members (nuclear/extended) are separate ways of classifying.
